ai.description: This frog measures 22–25 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale belly. Key features include a blunt snout and granular skin on the dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Philautus namdaphaensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored W-shaped mark on its back, which is absent in other similar Indian bush frogs.
ai.habitat: *Philautus namdaphaensis* inhabits the tropical evergreen forests of the Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh, typically found at altitudes around 300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Tirap bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the vegetation of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Philautus namdaphaensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Philautus namdaphaensis* is endemic to the Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh, India, found at elevations of approximately 400 meters within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Philautus namdaphaensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in dense evergreen forests.
